name: Western Branch librarianship training
description: A segregated public library trained African American library workers.

date.basis: Date of the documented episode, not a universal origin.

events.statement: Thomas Fountain Blue began a training program in librarianship for African Americans at the Western Branch, later also operated with Rachel Harris.
events.scope: Louisville program; segregation restricted professional opportunity.

evidence.supports: Dates Blue’s librarianship training program from 1912, later with Harris.

date.basis: Year on the branch brochure, reporting trainees to date.

events.statement: The library described a three-month apprentice class entered by examination and reported that twelve people had taken the course.
events.scope: 1915 brochure account, a cumulative count rather than annual enrollment.

evidence.supports: Describes entrance examination, three months of work, and twelve trainees by the account date.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented episode in this scoped record, not a global origin.

caveats: The 1915 brochure describes an examination but does not establish complete admission criteria, tuition or employment outcomes.

research.note: Initial source pass. Independent review checked the University of Southern Mississippi history and the 1915-era branch brochure: twelve people had taken the three-month course, and Harris’s role is later than Blue’s start.

measures.quantity: people who had taken apprentice course
measures.subject: Western Branch apprentice class
measures.conditions: Cumulative to the 1915 brochure, not a graduation or annual count.

evidence.supports: Describes entrance examination, three months of work, and twelve trainees by the account date.
